title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Factory on 1969-02-15
lineage: SBD > MR > Cassette > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a powerful 1969 performance with searing Dark Star, an intense The Other One and a standout Alligator‑Caution jam.
ai_review.review: The show is praised as a quintessential late‑'60s Dead experience, highlighted by a gothic‑like Dark Star, a brooding The Other One, and the epic Alligator → Drums → Alligator → Caution sequence.  Audio quality is described as good for the era – a clear soundboard source with occasional cuts that detract from a few jams but do not ruin the overall listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating is ~4.3 across 19 reviews; most comments are enthusiastic about the performance and note only minor recording issues, giving a strong positive consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced for the period; reviewers mention “good audio quality” and crisp sound.  A few note noticeable edits/cuts (especially around the Eleven and Death Don't) and a single comment rates the sound ~6.5/10, but no major drop‑outs are reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe an opening rag that builds into cosmic folk material, a strong second set that rockets through intense jams and seamless transitions, though later edits truncate some highlights.  Overall the concert is seen as a journey from raw early‑night energy to a powerful, improvisational climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for searing guitar work, strong vocals and “ripping” solos throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for rhythmic conversation with Jerry’s guitars, especially during the extended Dark Star section.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard playing highlighted as “great organ” in Dark Star; no specific player named.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as intense and “snarling,” with a memorable cowbell accent and feedback‑filled drum break.
